result.instructions: Tools for Runpod, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Which of my Pods are running right now, and what GPU does each one use?"; "Stop the Pod I left running overnight."; "How much did I spend on Pods this week, by day?". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Runpod data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run runpod_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run runpod_request_feature to record the request. Paid plans: Pro (10,000 tool calls a month, $9/month or $90/year, for normal use) and Pro+ (100,000 tool calls a month, $39/month or $390/year, for automations and heavy use). A plan can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run runpod_upgrade without a plan: it returns both plans, each with a payment link for the user to open. runpod_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: runpod_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: Get the Runpod account that owns the API key: its id and email. Good first call to confirm which account is connected. GET /v2/account.

tools.name: runpod_get_account_limits
tools.title: Get account limits
tools.description: Read the spend rate limit, current spend rate and resource limits of the account before deploying. GET /v2/account/limits.

tools.name: runpod_get_balance
tools.title: Get balance
tools.description: Read the account balance and billing mode (how much credit is left). GET /v2/billing/balance.

tools.name: runpod_get_billing_history
tools.title: Get billing history
tools.description: Get total spend over time across Pods, Serverless, storage and clusters, in time buckets. Use last_n for the most recent buckets. GET /v2/billing.

bucket_size.description: Length of each billing bucket. Default: day.

last_n.description: Return the last N buckets, ending with the current one.

tools.name: runpod_get_pod_billing
tools.title: Get Pod billing
tools.description: Get time-bucketed billing for one Pod or for all Pods: GPU, CPU, disk and total. GET /v2/billing/pods.

pod_id.description: Only this Pod id. Omit for all Pods.

bucket_size.description: Length of each billing bucket. Default: day.

last_n.description: Return the last N buckets, ending with the current one.

tools.name: runpod_list_pods
tools.title: List Pods
tools.description: List Pods owned by the account, with status, GPU, image and cost fields. Use cursor to get more pages. GET /v2/pods.

include_cluster_pods.description: Include cluster member Pods. Default: false.

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page's pagination.nextCursor. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: runpod_get_pod
tools.title: Get a Pod
tools.description: Get one Pod by id: compute, container, storage, networking, lifecycle status and connection details. GET /v2/pods/{id}.

tools.name: runpod_set_pod_state
tools.title: Start or stop a Pod
tools.description: Start or stop one Pod. A stopped Pod is not billed for compute, but its volume disk still bills. Starting a running Pod or stopping a stopped Pod changes nothing. POST /v2/pods/{id}/action.

tools.name: runpod_terminate_pod
tools.title: Terminate a Pod
tools.description: PERMANENTLY terminate one Pod: compute is released and its host-local persistent storage is destroyed. A network volume is only detached, not deleted. Cannot be undone. Cluster Pods cannot be terminated here. DELETE /v2/pods/{id}.

tools.name: runpod_list_serverless_endpoints
tools.title: List Serverless endpoints
tools.description: List Serverless endpoints owned by the account, with compute, worker limits, scaling and deployment settings. GET /v2/serverless.

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page's pagination.nextCursor. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: runpod_get_serverless_endpoint
tools.title: Get a Serverless endpoint
tools.description: Get one Serverless endpoint by id: compute, workers, scaling, container and current status. GET /v2/serverless/{id}.

tools.name: runpod_list_endpoint_workers
tools.title: List endpoint workers
tools.description: List the active workers of one Serverless endpoint, with status, runtime and counts by status. GET /v2/serverless/{id}/workers.

tools.name: runpod_get_endpoint_request_metrics
tools.title: Get endpoint request metrics
tools.description: Get request counts, execution time and queue delay of one Serverless endpoint as a time series. GET /v2/serverless/{id}/metrics/requests.

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page's pagination.nextCursor. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: runpod_list_templates
tools.title: List templates
tools.description: List the reusable Pod and Serverless templates owned by the account, with container, storage, port and environment settings. GET /v2/templates.

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page's pagination.nextCursor. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: runpod_get_template
tools.title: Get a template
tools.description: Get one template by id (owned or public): its container and deploy settings. GET /v2/templates/{id}.

tools.name: runpod_list_network_volumes
tools.title: List network volumes
tools.description: List the persistent network volumes owned by the account, with size, data center and storage tier. GET /v2/network-volumes.

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page's pagination.nextCursor. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: runpod_list_gpu_types
tools.title: List GPU types
tools.description: List GPU types with pricing. Set include_availability to see stock for a product, GPU count and cloud type. GET /v2/catalog/gpus.

include_availability.description: Add stock and lowest-price data. Needs product.

country_codes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, for example FR or FR,DE.

tools.name: runpod_list_data_centers
tools.title: List data centers
tools.description: List Runpod data centers with region, compliance and storage details. Filter by region or compliance. GET /v2/catalog/datacenters.

include_gpu_availability.description: Add current GPU availability per data center.

compliance.description: Compliance labels that must all match, for example GDPR or SOC_2_TYPE_2.

tools.name: runpod_list_audit_logs
tools.title: List audit logs
tools.description: List the audit trail: who did what to which resource and when. Filter by action, actor, time range or search text. GET /v2/audit-logs.

actions.description: Only these action names, exactly as recorded.

actor_ids.description: Only these user ids (organization accounts only).

search.description: Case-insensitive text match on email, resource, action or value.

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page's pagination.nextCursor. Omit for the first page.

prompts.name: getting_started
prompts.title: Get started with Runpod
prompts.description: What you can do with Runpod here, with example requests to try.

prompts.name: check_which_pods_run_and_what_they_cost
prompts.title: Check which Pods run and what they cost
prompts.description: List the Pods and open one to see its GPU, container and status. Read the billing of each Pod by time bucket.

prompts.name: review_spend_and_balance
prompts.title: Review spend and balance
prompts.description: Read the account balance and the billing mode. Read the billing history of Pods, Serverless and storage in time buckets.

prompts.name: check_gpu_stock_before_a_deploy
prompts.title: Check GPU stock before a deploy
prompts.description: Read the account limits. List the GPU types with their prices and availability, and the data centers in a region.

prompts.name: check_a_serverless_endpoint_under_load
prompts.title: Check a Serverless endpoint under load
prompts.description: Open one Serverless endpoint and list its active workers. Read its request counts and queue delay over time.

prompts.name: start_or_stop_a_pod
prompts.title: Start or stop a Pod
prompts.description: Start a stopped Pod, or stop a running one. A stopped Pod does not bill compute, but its volume disk still bills.

prompts.name: terminate_a_pod_permanently
prompts.title: Terminate a Pod permanently
prompts.description: Terminate a Pod to release its compute. This cannot be undone: host-local storage is destroyed. A network volume is only detached.
